key_insight: CARS uses centerline-anchored attention to predict coronary pressure and velocity in 87 ms per case, versus 572–1,063 s for CFD.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate enables rapid estimation of coronary flow and pressure-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) on skeleton-generated lumen geometries.
method: Inputs: image-derived centerline, per-point lumen radius, and scalar inlet flow rate.
Uses the case’s centerline as attention keys/values to predict pressure and velocity at arbitrary query points.
Geometry fusion scales as O(N n_f), rather than O(N²), for N query points and n_f centerline focal points.
evidence_signal: Trained per territory on 2,700 OpenFOAM solutions, CARS achieved left/right relative ℓ₂ errors of 0.120/0.063 for pressure and 0.149/0.119 for velocity, with 97.7%/96.3% agreement on held-out FFR ≤ 0.8 decisions.
watch_item: Predicted velocity is insufficiently continuity-consistent for derived quantities, and model weights are territory-specific.
paper_title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
